newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures closed down on Monday due to profit-taking triggered by last Friday's losses on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active April 1997 contract ended at 20,570 yuan ($2,478) per tonne, losing 240 yuan. It opened at an intra-day high of 20,600 and hit a low of 20,500.
January fell 40 to 20,260, February 140 to 20,350, March 210 to 20,450, May 240 to 20,580 and June 100 to 20,600.
Combined volume rose to 56,550 tonnes from 34,736.
Copper opened lower on LME losses and moved in a narrow range at low levels for most of the session.
Traders said profit-taking dominated today's trading with many short position holders also liquidating their positions.
"LME losses discouraged long position holders in Shanghai and profit-taking dominated trading for most of the session," one trader said.
"Open interest of all contracts dropped today, indicating investors were not willing to trade around the year-end, especially when the short-term market trend is so unclear," a second trader said.
Analysts expect copper to move around 20,500 yuan in the next few days.
Aluminium ended mixed. January fell 10 to 13,940 yuan per tonne, February 50 to 14,200 but March rose 50 to 14,450.
Combined volume fell to 470 tonnes from 2,340.
